title: A Real-Time Biomechanical Center-of-Mass Estimation System for Squat Assessment Using RGB-D Skeletal Sensing
content: As the knowledge of the posture adopted during a squat is essential for the im-provement of strength and endurance, and the prevention of injury, it is therefore neces-sary to have a correct and accurate determination of it. Although recent improvements in the accuracy of the measurements of the movements of the human body without the aid of a marker have produced remarkable results, yet few of these devices take into account the biomechanics of the whole body. This study introduces a new method for determining the position of the center of mass (COM) of the body, which uses the 3D skeletal data from a Microsoft Kinect V2 and an estimation model based on anthropometrically-determined segment masses to estimate the sagittal center during squatting. Stability is assessed using COM displacement in relation to the base of support and combined hip and knee angles to detect potential instability patterns related to sports injuries. The framework is designed to detect human skeletal motion in real time, and using a visual feedback interface it can de-termine the squatting posture as stable or unstable. It was found that this approach was able to track the skeleton in real-time, estimate the changes in COM during squatting, and give feedback about the COM and about the body stability. The COM estimations com-pared to joint angle-based evaluations provided more biomechanically meaningful evalu-ations of whole-body stability, and the system required less hardware and computational resources. It therefore offers a practical solution to intelligent fitness, home exercise, reha-bilitation engineering, and digital health care applications.
